Americans believe in rule of law —and the courts are saying that due process is required. If a president can ignore the courts and disappear lawful residents, there is no limit to what can come next. President Trump has said he wants to abduct and deport U.S. citizens. If this isn’t stopped now, no one is safe.

A key focal point of this campaign will be to call on local sheriffs to refuse to cooperate with directives from ICE to engage in federal immigration enforcement, such as renting jail beds to ICE, participating in immigration raids, and transferring people to ICE detentions.  Sheriffs have wide discretion in how much they cooperate with ICE. title: Bellaire Braeswood Democrats - Monthly Meeting
description:
Join us for an important update by Nicole Pedersen - HCDP Executive Director, on plans for the 2025-2026 Cycle.

Nicole Pedersen is the Executive Director of the Harris County Democratic Party. She was promoted to that position following the 2024 election. Prior to that, she held the position of Voter Protection Director. She began working with HCDP's Voter Protection program in 2018. In 2019, she served as the Voter Protection Director for Mayor Turner's re-election campaign and then returned to HCDP. Under her leadership, the Voter Protection program has grown to become the most robust countywide partisan voter protection program in Texas, encompassing the poll watcher program, lawyer's boileroom, voter hotline, and election worker supplemental training program. She received her law degree from the University of Chicago. She began her career as a corporate litigator in New York City, but has spent the majority of her decades in law helping people and companies understand and comply with various regulatory regimes. When not working at HCDP, Ms. Pedersen runs an international trade compliance law practice.

description:
Welcome to budget season in the PA General Assembly. Phew, are we here already?

We’ve invited State Reps. Jessica Benham (HD-36, Allegheny County) and Lindsay Powell (HD-21, Allegheny County) to discuss it at length on Thursday, June 12 at 8:30 AM and would love if you’d join us. 

What’s up with the budget anyway?
—It’s due by the end of June. This doesn’t always happen, but we’re hopeful that it will

—There are two types of budgets passed each year: a General Appropriations bill and a Codes bill – we’ll discuss the difference

—After Shapiro’s budget address in February, House and Senate Appropriations committees held budget hearings, which turn into close-door negotiation sessions — we want to know what they’ve been discussing

—Lawmakers typically amend existing bills to fit into the scope of the House or Senate Appropriations committees’ budget legislation

With both Rep. Powell and Rep. Benham sitting on various committees, we’re certain they will offer insights into how legislators are progressing some key issues such as Medicare/Medicaid, transportation, housing, climate change and more.

We look forward to answering questions posted in the chat during this briefing. If you can’t make it or want to send us a question in advance, please email us at info@representpa.org.

This briefing will be hosted by Represent PA’s Executive Director, Erin Belitskus.
